pretreatments.description: Hydrothermal pretreatment (HP) of sugarcane bagasse (SB) using autohydrolysis, performed at 183 °C, 41 minutes, and a liquid-to-solid ratio (LSR) of 3.94 mL g^−1, generating a liquor rich in C5 sugars and xylooligomers. Subsequently, low molar mass lignin fragments were partially removed by alkaline extraction (AE). Acid-catalyzed or organosolv methods were not used for delignification; the residual lignin remained chemically modified. The pretreated solid was further subjected to advanced oxidative pretreatment (AOP) to achieve high cellulose preservation and enzymatic conversion.

Alkaline extraction (AE) performed on HP-treated SB to remove low molar mass lignin fragments, consisting of an aqueous 0.2 mol L^−1 NaOH solution at a liquid-to-solid ratio (LSR) of 10 mL g^−1, speed of 2,800 rpm for 30 seconds. Aqueous washing with tap water was used to reach neutral pH before storage.

Advanced oxidative pretreatment (AOP) applied to alkaline-extracted pretreated SB using a 2 L white acrylic cylindrical reactor, involving an aqueous H_2O_2 solution at defined LSR and pH adjusted to 11.6, stirred at 150 rpm and 25 °C. Reaction time varied from 1 to 8 h based on experimental design, optimizing the application of H_2O_2 load (0.3-3.0 g_H2O2 g_SB^−1), LSR (5-25 mL g^−1), and reaction time. The process aimed to maximize degree of delignification (DE) and enzymatic conversion (EC) while minimizing yield loss (Y) and weight loss.
